relevance_note: Case report of a girl with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant, also found in her father and paternal uncle: "We identified a heterozygous variant in TNFAIP3, namely NM_006290.4:c.460G > T".
method_note: Read the whole paper (no tables, no supplementary section); built the JSON by hand in a short Python script and checked every span verbatim against the Markdown (variant uses thin spaces around '>', doses use four-per-em spaces). Seven in-scope people: the patient (single unnamed proband, label 'patient'), the father and the father's brother (both carry the same TNFAIP3 variant), the mother (screened for TNFAIP3; the variant is of paternal origin, so she gets no variant row), and three untested paternal-line relatives described with conditions (paternal grandfather, brother of paternal grandfather, father's uncle), whom the paper says 'presented potential clinical conditions of HA20'. Relative labels use the relation as written relative to the patient ('father's brother' is also called 'paternal uncle' once). 'Father's uncle' and 'brother of paternal grandfather' are listed separately in the paper and kept as two people. The heterozygous TNFRSF13B variant (patient, maternal; mother) is called a 'known risk allele' and is not listed, per the scope rule on risk alleles. The paper says the father's brother had 'the same mutations' (plural) in TNFAIP3; recorded as the same single variant. Zygosity and inheritance not stated for the father and his brother. n_patients_reported left null: the authors give no count (they speak of one patient, but three TNFAIP3 carriers are described). The patient's age 'one-year-old' is her age at presentation, not at last evaluation or diagnosis, so those fields are 'not reported'. 'VES' (normal) is unexplained in the paper; its HPO candidate (ESR) is my reading. CRP was elevated while VES was normal; the composite inflammatory-marker item is observed on CRP. The patient had one reported febrile episode, so 'recurrent fever' is not reported. Steroid side effects (weight gain, mood/behaviour change, diabetes) are recorded as observed features but 'type 1 diabetes' is not reported. Anemia was attributed to gastrointestinal bleeding, so 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' is not reported. Colonic lymphoid nodular hyperplasia was only 'suggestive' macroscopically and is not counted as lymphoproliferation. Normal ANCA/ASCA do not exclude 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' (ANA not addressed). Father's vitiligo not counted under the 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)' item. No contradictions found; the abstract's 'since childhood' for the father is consistent with the Discussion's 'presented later in life' (relative to the patient's infantile onset).
